title: IsHaunted Device Data Format v1
description: A single capture session from one investigation device. See DeviceDataFormat-v1.md for the prose specification and rationale.

format_version.description: Semantic version of THIS format, not of the device firmware. Consumers accept any 1.x.

device.description: What produced the readings. Identifies the instrument, not the operator.

serial_number.description: Null when the device has none or the operator declined to record it.

session.description: When and where this capture happened, and how readings were triggered.

started_at.description: UTC, ISO-8601 with offset. When the capture session began.

device_powered_on_at.description: UTC. Lets a consumer judge warm-up drift on instruments that need it.

battery_percent_at_start.description: 0-100. Low battery is a known source of spurious readings on several EMF meters.

property_area.description: Optional structured area tag, for grouping across sessions and devices.

timezone.description: IANA name of the local zone the operator was working in. Timestamps stay UTC; this is only so a consumer can render local time as the operator experienced it.

trigger.description: How readings came to be recorded. Determines whether gaps mean 'nothing happened' or 'not sampled'.

interval_seconds.description: Required for interval and hybrid. The sampling period, or the heartbeat period under hybrid.

event_description.description: Required for event and hybrid. Plain language: what causes a record. 'motion detected on PIR', 'field exceeds 2.0 uT'.

debounce_seconds.description: Minimum quiet period between event records. Null means the device does not debounce.

readings.description: The records themselves, ordered oldest first. May be empty — a session where nothing triggered is still evidence.

reading.description: One record. Every field except the timestamp is optional: devices report what they can.

precision.description: Meaningful resolution of 'at'. A device stamping whole seconds must say so rather than implying millisecond accuracy it does not have.

sequence.description: Device-assigned counter. Lets a consumer detect dropped records that timestamps alone would hide.

triggered_by.description: Why this particular record exists. Under hybrid, distinguishes a heartbeat from a real event.

measurements.description: Device-specific channels, keyed by channel name. The extension point — new instruments add keys here, never new top-level fields.

audio_ref.description: Companion audio for this moment, if the device captured any.

note.description: Operator's free-text remark attached to this record.

measurement.description: One measured channel. Unit is required whenever a value is present — a bare number is not evidence.

unit.description: Symbol as written: 'uT', 'degC', 'lux', 'dBA', '%'. ASCII only, so encoding can't corrupt it.

accuracy.description: Plus-or-minus, in the same unit as value.

baseline.description: The ambient reference this device was calibrated against, same unit. Turns an absolute number into a deviation.

out_of_range.description: True when the reading hit the sensor's limit and the real value is unknown.

position.description: Where the device was. Indoor GPS is usually poor — accuracy_meters is how a consumer knows whether to trust it.

floor.description: Building floor. 0 = ground, negative = below ground.

motion.description: How the device was moving. A field spike while the meter was being swung is a different fact from one while it sat still.

is_stationary.description: Device's own judgement, when it makes one.

file_ref.description: A companion file shipped alongside the JSON.

filename.description: Relative path within the delivered bundle. Never absolute, never traversing upward.

start_offset_seconds.description: Where in the file this reading's moment falls, when the file covers a span.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex digest of the file, so a consumer can prove the pairing survived transit.
